clue.text: Kremlin: it's captured by rebel, a first for Lenin

indicators.note: being captured by something means being held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450
'it' taken as written; the 's is 'is', a link

indicators.note: a first for Lenin is the opening letter of that name

explanation.surface: A rebel seizes the Kremlin, a first for Lenin's old seat of power.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a peasants' revolt in England in 1450, a stock crossword rebel; the 's of it's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified citadel at the heart of Moscow, so it is a specific example of the type.

clue.text: Fearsome creature about — many scattered

parts.note: ca (circa) means about

indicators.note: scattered letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fearsome beast with many prey scattered about.
explanation.walkthrough: CA, short for the Latin circa, is a standard way of writing 'about' with dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A cayman is a Central and South American crocodilian, the kind of animal one would fear.

clue.text: Fitting shapes on surface, mathematician's about following

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: Alan Turing was the British mathematician; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A mathematician works on fitting shapes together over a surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TURING around F.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying sods of grass, cut shapes of turf, on bare ground is the gardener's sense of the verb.

clue.text: Barrier to a view of very ancient city

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
a scene is a view

explanation.surface: A wall blocks the view of an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene is the adjective for Damascus, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

clue.text: Join clubs released from prison

indicators.note: the letter for clubs is let out of the word for prison, so it is removed

parts.note: clink is slang for prison
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A gang of clubs freed from prison join up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'released from' takes C out of CLINK.
explanation.definitionFit: To link two things is to connect or fasten them together, a synonym for join.

clue.text: Stressed one's too drunk to go to bed?

definitions.text: one's too drunk to go to bed?
definitions.meaning: read cryptically: still 'up' (not in bed) and 'tight' (drunk)

explanation.surface: A tense reveller is too far gone even to make it to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into UP, meaning not yet in bed, and TIGHT, slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Being highly strung and anxious is what it means to be tense in this informal adjective.

clue.text: How intellectual's head goes? No, Lord Copper

definitions.meaning: a highbrow is called a pointy-head, so the head rises to a sharp tip
in Evelyn Waugh's Scoop, staff dare not say 'No' to the press baron Lord Copper and use a polite stock phrase instead

explanation.surface: A remark on the shape of an egghead's skull, then an employee contradicting the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Copper is the tyrannical newspaper owner in Waugh's novel Scoop; his underling says 'Up to a point, Lord Copper' to mean 'No'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is true only partly is a tactful way of disagreeing, which is the sense of the phrase here.

clue.text: Wrong end of the cake

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone has the wrong end of the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered gateau, so it is a kind of cake.

clue.text: Try to chuck young bird …

parts.note: a go is a try
sling means chuck, throw

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to throw a young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A gosling is a baby goose, so it is a young bird.

clue.text: … try to keep countryman very stupid

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: test means try
a hick is an unsophisticated country person

explanation.surface: Following on, a test holds a dim country bumpkin.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the one before, both opening on 'try', but here it means test rather than go.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickest is the superlative of thick, slang for dull-witted, so it means extremely stupid.

clue.text: Church wants to dismiss priest, becoming one short

parts.note: in cricket to york a batsman is to bowl him out with a yorker, so dismiss him

indicators.note: falling short of one means lacking that letter, so it is removed

parts.note: a minister is a clergyman
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A church plans to sack its priest, leaving it a man down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to york' is a cricket term: to bowl a batsman out with a ball pitched at his feet. 'short' with 'one' removes I from MINISTER, leaving MINSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: York Minster is the great Gothic cathedral of York, so it is a famous example of a church.

clue.text: Whizz down slope — take-off finally aborted

indicators.note: its final letter is aborted, cut off from the end of the word

parts.note: a skit is a parody or take-off

explanation.surface: A plane's take-off is aborted at the last moment as something whizzes down a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' sounds like aviation but means a parody, a SKIT; 'finally aborted' drops its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing is gliding rapidly downhill on runners, so the verb fits the phrase about whizzing down a slope.

clue.text: In a dark back street

indicators.note: back signals the word for dark is read backwards

parts.note: dim means dark

explanation.surface: Someone lurks in a dark back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DIM into MID.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst is a preposition meaning in the middle of, so it can stand for in.

clue.text: Michael carries state as an Independent

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Mick is a short form of Michael
aver means state firmly

explanation.surface: A man named Michael carries a whole state's vote while standing as an independent candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a US state or a nation but is the verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an unorthodox individualist who stands apart from any group, which is an independent in the noun sense.

clue.text: Troublesome Pets' Annual needs editing

indicators.note: editing reworks text, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly written yearbook about pets needs an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs editing' rearranges PETS and ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troublesome causes bother or discomfort, which is close to disagreeable or nasty.

clue.text: Enough grease's churned out that will affect the climate

indicators.note: churned means stirred up and mixed, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: So much grease is churned out that it will change the climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churned out' rearranges ENOUGH and GREASES (the apostrophe ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon dioxide and methane trap heat in the atmosphere, warming the planet, which is how they affect the climate.

clue.text: Farmhand keeps drink in crock

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sherd or potsherd is a broken piece of crockery
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A farm worker stores his drink in an earthenware pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crock' is a piece of broken pottery here, not an old wreck; sherd is a variant of shard.
explanation.definitionFit: A swineherd tends pigs, so he is a kind of farm labourer.

clue.text: Side of cricket field (leg) not visible from house

parts.note: the off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman
a stage is a leg of a journey

explanation.surface: One half of a cricket ground, the leg side, cannot be seen from the pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' in brackets looks like the cricket field's other side, but it is a stage of a journey. The off side is one half of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, actors offstage are out of sight of the house, which means the audience.

clue.text: A grounding in emergency procedure

parts.note: reads like basic training in what to do in a crisis, but describes an aircraft being brought to the ground in an emergency

explanation.surface: Trainees are given a basic grounding in what to do in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounding' looks like elementary instruction but literally means coming down to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft forced down by an emergency touches ground under duress, and that literal grounding is the whole description.

clue.text: Boy grabbed by lecher in passage not easy to negotiate

indicators.note: grabbed by means held inside the other piece

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is seized by a lecher in a narrow passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' is musical, not a corridor: a roulade is a florid vocal run.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rapid run of notes sung to one syllable, a demanding musical passage.

clue.text: Girl, one crazy for braid

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a loon is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A girl, rather mad, longs for braid.
explanation.definitionFit: Galloon is a narrow ornamental trimming of lace or braid used to edge clothing.

clue.text: Grounds to show data is in error

indicators.note: in error means wrong, so the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: There are grounds for showing the data is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges DATA and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia, plural of stadium, are sports grounds.

clue.text: Stop chap growing double

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: to stunt is to stop growing, and a man is a chap
a film double who stands in for an actor in dangerous scenes

explanation.surface: A command to keep some young fellow from getting any bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part splits the answer: STUNT, to stop something growing, and MAN, a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who replaces a star for risky action scenes is a stand-in, the film sense of a double.

clue.text: Where in the States a trollop's brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: slut is a crude synonym for trollop; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A question about where in America a loose woman was raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses A SLUT. Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma, so it is a place in the United States.

clue.text: Dog, say, keeping four feet not quite in shot

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet
an ell was an old measure of cloth, 45 inches, just under four feet

explanation.surface: A dog is held nearly four feet back from a gunshot.
explanation.walkthrough: The English ell of 45 inches is three and three-quarter feet, so not quite four.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a small piece of lead shot fired from a shotgun.

clue.text: Esau's people do me wrong

indicators.note: doing wrong to something here means jumbling its letters

explanation.surface: Esau's people wrong me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges DO and ME.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau was also called Edom, and his descendants the Edomites formed the nation of that name.

clue.text: Listen to help a woman

indicators.note: asks us to hear the words, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: help is aid, followed by a: 'aid a'

explanation.surface: An instruction to heed a plea for help from a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: AID A said aloud sounds like the name Ada.
explanation.definitionFit: Ada is a female given name, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Money offered to dame to keep? This is new!

parts.note: a loan is money offered to a borrower
a DBE is a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire
hold means keep

explanation.surface: Someone lends money to an older lady for safekeeping and calls it a novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: DBE is the British honour that makes a woman a Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation drawing attention to something surprising or newly seen, much like crying out at a novelty.

clue.text: Relied on English staying good and tasteful

indicators.note: the letter for good is staying within the word for relied on, held inside it

parts.note: leant means relied on

explanation.surface: Someone relied on the English staying well-behaved and refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staying' puts G inside LEANT, giving LEGANT, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish, which is what tasteful describes.

clue.text: Mary's wonderful food — make to tuck in

definitions.note: Mary is, with the 's as 'is' linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: tucking in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: manna was the miraculous food from heaven in Exodus
do means make, as in do a meal

explanation.surface: Mary's food is wonderful, so make sure to tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Mary's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay; manna fell from heaven to feed the Israelites.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madonna is the title of the Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus.
